name: Political instability
value: Indonesia VP resigns 12 Nov; no G20 collapse
summary: Indonesia's vice-president resigned on 12 Nov ahead of an impeachment motion; the government is not at risk of collapse
state: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on 12 Nov, hours before parliament was due to consider an impeachment petition over his eligibility; President Prabowo accepted it and the MPR may take up to 60 days to choose a successor (ABC). The same day police said a former police chief was the end user of illegal wiretaps on Prabowo and that treason charges are being considered (The Star). This is a constitutional succession, not a government collapse, and no G20 coup or contested election was found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Investors, firms and travellers with exposure to Indonesia may see policy uncertainty while the vice-presidency is vacant; travellers can check FCDO advice on protests in Indonesian cities.
rubric_hit: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in past month (Normal); Indonesia VP resignation is orderly

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.

rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.
